title: Build a league table without touching the caller's list

blocks.text: The league site shows standings in three places. The club pages pass the teams in fixture order and draw the fixture list from that same list afterwards. The results importer passes a list it keeps adding teams to as results come in. The public API passes a list that nobody may change.

Finish `table(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Standings.java`: the teams by points, most first, with teams on the same points in the order they were given. Every caller must get its table and find its own list as it left it, and a table it already holds must not change when its list does later. About three lines in total.

cases.says: the table lists the teams by points, most first, with level teams in the order given
the list the caller passed is in its original order after the call
an unmodifiable list of teams gets a table instead of an exception
a table already returned doesn't change when the caller later changes its own list

origin.section: A Method That Changes Its Argument Makes That Change Part of Its Contract

concepts: A method that changes its argument changes the caller's object, so a method that only reads its input works on its own copy.
